extracted_concepts.name: Limit
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Value approached by a function as the input approaches a point.

extracted_concepts.name: One-sided Limit
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Limit approached from the left or right side.

extracted_concepts.name: Limit at Infinity
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Limit of a function as x grows without bound.

extracted_concepts.name: Continuity at a Point
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A function is continuous at a if lim_{x→a} f(x) = f(a).

extracted_concepts.name: Removable Discontinuity
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A discontinuity that can be repaired by redefining a point.

extracted_concepts.name: Horizontal Asymptote
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Horizontal line approached by a graph as x tends to infinity.

extracted_concepts.name: Vertical Asymptote
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Vertical line where a function grows without bound.

extracted_concepts.name: Squeeze Theorem
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: If g(x) ≤ f(x) ≤ h(x) and lim g = lim h = L, then lim f = L.

extracted_concepts.name: Limit Laws
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Sum, difference, product, and quotient rules for limits.

extracted_concepts.name: Average Rate of Change
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Change in output divided by change in input over an interval.

extracted_concepts.name: Instantaneous Rate of Change
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Rate of change at a single instant.

extracted_concepts.name: Tangent Line
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Line touching a curve at a point with slope f'(a).

extracted_concepts.name: Secant Line
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Line through two points on a curve representing average rate.

extracted_concepts.name: Differentiability
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Existence of a derivative at a point.

extracted_concepts.name: Power Rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: d/dx(x^n) = nx^{n-1}.

extracted_concepts.name: Product Rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: (fg)' = f'g + fg'.

extracted_concepts.name: Implicit Differentiation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Differentiating equations not solved for y.

extracted_concepts.name: Inverse Function Derivative Rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: If y = f(x) and x = g(y), then g'(y) = 1/f'(g(y)).

extracted_concepts.name: Higher-Order Derivative
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Derivatives of derivatives, such as f'', f''', f^{(n)}.

extracted_concepts.name: L'Hospital's Rule
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: For 0/0 or ∞/∞, lim f/g = lim f'/g'.

extracted_concepts.name: Mean Value Theorem
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: f'(c) = [f(b)-f(a)]/(b-a) for some c in (a,b).

extracted_concepts.name: Extreme Value Theorem
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: A continuous function on [a,b] has absolute max and min.

extracted_concepts.name: Critical Point
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Point where f' is zero or undefined.

extracted_concepts.name: First Derivative Test
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Classifies critical points using sign changes of f'.

extracted_concepts.name: Second Derivative Test
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Uses f''(c) to classify local extrema at critical points.

extracted_concepts.name: Concavity
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: f'' > 0 gives concave up; f'' < 0 gives concave down.

extracted_concepts.name: Optimization
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Finding maximum or minimum values subject to constraints.

extracted_concepts.name: Riemann Sum
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Sum approximating area using rectangles.

extracted_concepts.name: Definite Integral
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: ∫_a^b f(x)dx = lim Σ f(x_i*)Δx.

extracted_concepts.name: Fundamental Theorem of Calculus
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Connects derivatives and definite integrals.

extracted_concepts.name: Substitution
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Integration method reversing the chain rule.

extracted_concepts.name: Differential Equation
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Equation involving derivatives of a function.

extracted_concepts.name: Slope Field
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Visual representation of dy/dx for a differential equation.

extracted_concepts.name: Separation of Variables
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Method solving dy/dx by integrating separated variables.

extracted_concepts.name: Taylor Polynomial
extracted_concepts.definition_snippet: Polynomial approximation using derivatives at a point.

extracted_relations.evidence: One-sided limits refine the idea of a limit.
Limits at infinity are a type of limit.
Continuity requires lim_{x→a} f(x) = f(a).
Horizontal asymptotes are determined by limits at infinity.
Vertical asymptotes arise from unbounded one-sided limits.
The theorem determines a limit from bounding limits.
f'(a) is defined as a limit of difference quotients.
The derivative represents instantaneous rate of change.
The slope of a secant line is an average rate of change.
The tangent line slope at a point is f'(a).
Differentiability implies continuity.
The power rule computes derivatives of powers.
The product rule computes derivatives of products.
The quotient rule computes derivatives of quotients.
The chain rule differentiates composite functions.
Implicit differentiation often applies the chain rule to y.
Inverse derivative formulas rely on inverse-function and chain-rule reasoning.
Higher-order derivatives are repeated derivatives.
Linearization uses f'(a).
L'Hospital's Rule uses f'/g' for indeterminate limits.
The theorem guarantees a point where f' equals average rate.
The theorem applies to continuous functions on closed intervals.
The test classifies critical points using f'.
The test evaluates f'' at critical points.
Concavity is determined by f''.
Optimization uses derivatives to find extrema.
Newton's Method uses f'(x_n) in its iteration.
A definite integral is defined as a limit of Riemann sums.
The theorem evaluates definite integrals using antiderivatives.
u-substitution is described as the chain rule in reverse.
